about: Curve analyzer (docs/apcalc-spec.md section 6). The curves, scenes and every number live in calculus/assets/tools/math/curve-analyzer.js; contexts unlock with their topics. Checked by scripts/lib/apcalc-tool-checks/curve-analyzer.mjs.
intro: The graphs of $f$, $f'$ and $f''$, stacked on one $x$-axis and always in the same colors: crimson, blue, green. Drag across them and one cursor reads all three. The sign charts of $f'$ and $f''$ build themselves; critical points and points of inflection are marked on $f$, each with the sentence that justifies it. In Optimize, choose the size of a box, a field or a can and watch the quantity and its derivative.
howItWorks:
• Critical points are the interior $x$ where $f'(x) = 0$ or $f'(x)$ is undefined (with $f$ defined). Each curve's $f'$ and $f''$ are exact formulas, listed under Formulas & numbers.
  • First derivative test: a relative maximum where $f'$ changes from positive to negative, a relative minimum where it changes from negative to positive, neither where it keeps its sign (try the quartic at $x = 0$).
  • Inflection where $f''$ changes sign, that is, where $f'$ changes from increasing to decreasing or back.
  • Candidates test on the closed interval: compare $f$ at the endpoints and the critical points; the largest and smallest values are the absolute extrema.
  • Keyboard: on the graphs, the arrow keys move the cursor (Shift for bigger steps) and Page Up / Page Down jump to the next marked feature.
  • Optimize: the box is cut from a 12 in sheet, $V(x) = x(12 - 2x)^2$; the field uses 240 m of fence on three sides, $A(x) = x(240 - 2x)$; the can holds 355 cm³, $S(r) = 2\pi r^2 + \frac{710}{r}$.
